Academic project · Mechatronics

Design and construction of a pneumatic gripper

Diego Becerra Fuentes · Tecnológico de Monterrey · 2025
Pneumatics3D printing (PLA + TPU)Cobot end-effectorTIA Portal🏆 1st place

01Introduction

This project is a subsection of a larger one: the design, programming and construction of a collaborative-robot-powered mock industrial cell with industrial imaging and piece selection/rejection. One requirement was a custom mechanical gripper that attaches to the cobot, is controlled through industrial automation tools such as TIA Portal, and can carry a Schneider Electric circuit breaker.

Robotic grippers are end-effectors that let a robot arm interact with objects. They imitate the basic function of a human hand: pick up, hold, move and release with precision. Their design depends on the object’s shape, size, weight and material, and on the task.

MechanicalFingers or jaws that grasp the object. Electric, pneumatic or hydraulic actuation.
VacuumSuction for flat or smooth surfaces.
MagneticFor ferromagnetic materials.
SoftFlexible materials for delicate or irregular shapes.

In industry they appear in assembly lines, packaging, material handling, sorting and automated manufacturing.

02Design

The first decision was the gripper type. We chose a pneumatically actuated mechanical gripper, since the wider project gave us access to a controllable air pump. The design is centered on an MAL 80 mm × 25 mm double-acting cylinder. Double action avoids installing a return spring, which simplifies the gripper itself at the cost of more complex pneumatic wiring.

Single vs. double-acting cylinder

Pressurize a port and watch both cylinders respond at the same time.

Single acting (spring return)
Double acting

In the design, the cylinder sits inside a casing that also contains one of the gripper’s fingers; the piston rod connects to the other. Only one finger moves during operation, a choice made for mechanical simplicity.

03Construction

The body is 3D-printed PLA held together with M3 screws. The fingertips carry pads of softer 3D-printed TPU to grip objects better. The main challenge was designing parts that fit the pneumatic cylinder precisely: too loose and it rattles in operation, too tight and it risks damage.

ActuatorMAL 80 × 25 mm, double acting
BodyPLA, M3 fasteners
Fingertip padsTPU
ControlTIA Portal, pneumatic valves
PayloadSchneider Electric circuit breaker

04Conclusion

Thanks to its ease of manufacture and mechanical reliability, this gripper was one of the factors that led my team to win first place in the design and construction of a mock industrial cell with its digital twin.
